name: Mephibosheth
bio:
Mephibosheth was the son of Jonathan and grandson of Saul. He was five years old when news came of Saul and Jonathan's deaths at Jezreel; his nurse picked him up and fled in panic, and in her haste he fell and was crippled in both feet from then on (2 Samuel 4:4).

Years later, David asked whether anyone was left of Saul's house to whom he could show kindness for Jonathan's sake, and Saul's former servant Ziba told him of Mephibosheth, now living in the house of Machir son of Ammiel in Lo-debar. David sent for him; Mephibosheth came and fell on his face before the king, and when David said his name, he answered, "Your servant" (2 Samuel 9:1-6). David told him not to be afraid, restored to him all the land that had belonged to Saul, and declared that Mephibosheth would eat at the king's own table from then on — like one of the king's sons. Mephibosheth, overwhelmed, replied, "What is your servant, that you should notice a dead dog like me?" David then assigned Ziba and his household to farm the land on Mephibosheth's behalf, while Mephibosheth himself settled in Jerusalem, eating continually at the king's table, crippled in both feet to the end (2 Samuel 9:7-13). Mephibosheth's story continues during Absalom's rebellion, when his loyalty to David comes into painful question, told in detail in the chapters ahead.
